comment: Cross-platform vectors for recurring-expense rules: does a bank charge's merchant match a rule's pattern? Both implementations (TS: apps/web/src/lib/recurring.ts; Swift: RecurringRules.swift) MUST pass every case. Folding is the same as the bank matcher's: lowercase, accents stripped. A pattern with NO '*' matches as a SUBSTRING, which is how a person writes one; a pattern WITH '*' is anchored, which is how you tighten it when the substring is too loose.

matches.comment: pattern x merchant -> does it match

cases.name: a bare pattern is a substring, so it finds the merchant's own wording
and it is case-insensitive in both directions
accents fold, because the bank does not spell them
and fold the other way too
a substring that is not there does not match
trailing star anchors the start: Opal* is what the user wrote
...and that anchor is what makes it refuse a mid-word hit
leading star anchors the end
a star in the middle spans whatever is between
a star matches nothing at all, so the exact word still passes
two stars, both anchors gone: back to a substring
digits are part of the merchant and can be matched
spaces inside a pattern are literal
surrounding whitespace is trimmed, because it is a typo not an intent
an empty pattern matches NOTHING — it would otherwise claim every charge
a pattern of only stars matches nothing, for the same reason
an empty merchant is matched by nothing
regex characters are literal: a rule is not a regular expression
...and a dot is a dot

firstMatch.comment: When several rules match one charge, which one wins. Ordered by how specific the pattern is (longer wins), then by pattern so it is deterministic on both platforms — never by document id, which the two clients cannot agree on.

cases.name: the more specific pattern wins over the looser one
same length, so the alphabet decides and both clients agree
nothing matches, nothing is chosen

estimate.comment: When a rule carries no amount, the AUD is estimated from the bank's USD and the rate the household's own verified pairs reveal (BankMatch.learnRate). Integer cents, rounded half-up, because money is cents everywhere. A null rate means nothing has been verified yet and there is nothing to estimate from — the charge has to be asked about instead.

cases.name: the plain case: US$ 5,20 at 0.65 is $8,00
rounds to the nearest cent rather than truncating
rounds half up, so a half cent does not vanish
a rate above 1 is still just division
nothing verified yet, nothing to estimate from
a zero rate is not a rate
a negative rate is not a rate either
an estimate never comes out as zero — it would read as free

run.comment: One run of the rules over the pending charges: what gets FILED on its own and what gets ASKED. Both clients plan a run with this and nothing else — it used to be written twice, and it diverged twice in one day: iOS filed only newly arrived charges while the web filed everything claimable, and the web re-filed a charge somebody had just taken back with undo. A run happens only when a charge ARRIVES (`fresh` = pending minus `seen`); a rule made for a charge already waiting is applied by the rule dialog itself (claimsOfOneRule / addRecurringRuleAndApply), not here. Filing and asking are deliberately asymmetric: FILE everything claimable and priceable that this session has not filed — a charge can become priceable after it was first seen, once filing another teaches the rate — but ASK only about charges that just arrived, because re-opening a question somebody postponed is the app nagging. `filed` is what this session filed; an undo puts the charge back in pending and it must not be filed again. `pending`, `file` and `ask` are oldest first. amountAudCents null = the rule says 'ask me'.

cases.name: a charge that arrives, claimed by a rule with an amount, is filed at that amount
a charge that arrives, claimed by a rule with no amount and no rate, is asked about
with a learned rate, a rule with no amount files an estimate instead of asking
nothing arrived: nothing is filed or asked, even what is claimable
an arrival brings along a seen charge that has become priceable since
a charge this session filed and somebody undid is not filed again when the next one arrives
a postponed question is not asked again when an unrelated charge arrives
a charge no rule claims is only marked seen
two questions arriving together are both asked, oldest first
